coverage: All 43 sections of both local Hall-based English editions: named cast, genealogies, embedded tales, reviewed unnamed roles, named weapons and peoples; separate opening Beowulf and later kingship gate.

entities.name: Beowulf
entities.body: The poem’s hero, a Geatish warrior, son of Ecgtheow and nephew of King Hygelac.

snapshots.body: The poem’s hero, now king of the Geats; Ecgtheow’s son and Hygelac’s nephew.

entities.name: Beowulf, son of Scyld
entities.body: The early Danish ruler, son of Scyld and father of Healfdene; a different Beowulf from the poem’s hero.

entities.name: Hrothgar
entities.body: The Danish king who built Heorot, husband of Wealhtheow.

entities.name: Grendel
entities.body: The monster who attacks Hrothgar’s hall, Heorot.

entities.name: Grendel’s mother
entities.body: The unnamed mother of Grendel, who lives in the waters near the moors.

entities.name: The dragon
entities.body: The fire-breathing dragon guarding an ancient hoard in Geatland.

entities.name: Wiglaf
entities.body: The young warrior in Beowulf’s service, son of Weohstan and a kinsman of Beowulf.

entities.name: Hygelac
entities.body: The king of the Geats, Beowulf’s uncle and lord; spelled Higelac in this translation.

entities.name: Wealhtheow
entities.body: Hrothgar’s queen and the mother of Hrethric, Hrothmund and Freaware.

entities.name: Unferth
entities.body: Hrothgar’s courtier who challenges Beowulf’s reputation, son of Ecglaf.

entities.name: Wulfgar
entities.body: Hrothgar’s court officer who receives Beowulf’s party, a prince of the Wendels.

entities.name: Hygd
entities.body: Hygelac’s queen, daughter of Hæreth and mother of Heardred.

entities.name: Hrothulf
entities.body: Hrothgar’s nephew, raised in his household and seated beside him at the feast.

entities.name: Hrethric
entities.body: One of the sons of Hrothgar and Wealhtheow.

entities.name: Hrothmund
entities.body: One of the sons of Hrothgar and Wealhtheow.

entities.name: Freaware
entities.body: Hrothgar and Wealhtheow’s daughter, betrothed to Ingeld of the Heathobards.

entities.name: Hondscio
entities.body: One of Beowulf’s Geatish companions at Heorot.

entities.name: Æschere
entities.body: Hrothgar’s trusted adviser and companion in battle, elder brother of Yrmenlaf.

entities.name: Scyld Scefing
entities.body: The founding ruler of the Danish Scylding line in the poem’s opening.

entities.name: Healfdene
entities.body: The Danish king who is the father of Hrothgar, Heorogar, Halga and Elan.

entities.name: Heorogar
entities.body: Hrothgar’s elder brother and predecessor as Danish king, also called Heregar.

entities.name: Halga
entities.body: Hrothgar’s brother, one of Healfdene’s sons.

entities.name: Elan
entities.body: Hrothgar’s sister, identified in this translation as Ongentheow’s wife.

entities.name: Ongentheow
entities.body: The Swedish king, father of Onela and Ohthere, in the Geats’ history of their wars.

entities.name: Ecgtheow
entities.body: Beowulf’s father, who married King Hrethel’s daughter.

entities.name: Hrethel
entities.body: The former king of the Geats, Beowulf’s maternal grandfather and Hygelac’s father.

entities.name: Heatholaf
entities.body: The Wilfing warrior in Hrothgar’s account of Ecgtheow’s feud.

entities.name: Ecglaf
entities.body: Unferth’s father.

entities.name: Breca
entities.body: Beowulf’s youthful swimming rival, son of Beanstan and a lord of the Brondings.

entities.name: Beanstan
entities.body: Breca’s father.

entities.name: Wayland
entities.body: The legendary smith credited with making Beowulf’s armor.

entities.name: Sigmund
entities.body: The legendary hero praised in the court poet’s dragon-fighting tale.

entities.name: Fitela
entities.body: Sigmund’s nephew and companion in the tale recalled by the poet.

entities.name: Wæls
entities.body: Sigmund’s father, whose name appears in his family designation.

entities.name: Heremod
entities.body: The earlier Danish king used as a warning about a ruler’s pride and cruelty.

entities.name: Ecgwela
entities.body: An early Danish ruler whose people are recalled in Hrothgar’s warning.

entities.name: Finn
entities.body: The Frisian king in the hall-singer’s story, husband of Hildeburg.

entities.name: Hnæf
entities.body: The Danish leader in the Finn episode, Hildeburg’s brother.

entities.name: Hildeburg
entities.body: Finn’s Danish wife, sister of Hnæf and daughter of Hoce.

entities.name: Hoce
entities.body: The father of Hildeburg and Hnæf.

entities.name: Hengest
entities.body: The Danish warrior who leads Hnæf’s surviving men in the Finn episode.

entities.name: Folcwalda
entities.body: Finn’s father.

entities.name: Hun
entities.body: The Frisian in this translation who gives a sword to Hengest.

entities.name: Guthlaf
entities.body: One of Hnæf’s Danish warriors in the Finn episode.

entities.name: Oslaf
entities.body: One of Hnæf’s Danish warriors in the Finn episode.

entities.name: Hama
entities.body: The legendary hero who carries off the Brosingmen’s necklace in the poet’s comparison.

entities.name: Eormenric
entities.body: The king whose hostility Hama escapes in the necklace allusion.

entities.name: Swerting
entities.body: Hygelac’s ancestor, called his grandfather in this translation.

entities.name: Yrmenlaf
entities.body: Æschere’s younger brother.

entities.name: Hæreth
entities.body: Hygd’s father.

entities.name: Thrytho
entities.body: The queen in the poet’s contrast with Hygd, wife of Offa.

entities.name: Heming
entities.body: A kinsman named in the account of Offa and Eomær.

entities.name: Offa
entities.body: The legendary king of the Angles, husband of Thrytho and father of Eomær.

entities.name: Eomær
entities.body: The son of Offa and Thrytho, grandson of Garmund.

entities.name: Garmund
entities.body: Offa’s father and Eomær’s grandfather.

entities.name: Froda
entities.body: The Heathobard ruler who is Ingeld’s father.

entities.name: Ingeld
entities.body: The Heathobard prince betrothed to Hrothgar’s daughter Freaware.

entities.name: Hereward
entities.body: Heorogar’s son, named in the history of the armor Beowulf brings home.

entities.name: Heardred
entities.body: The son of Hygelac and Hygd, who succeeds his father as king of the Geats.

entities.name: Hereric
entities.body: Heardred’s uncle.

entities.name: Ohthere
entities.body: The Swedish prince, son of Ongentheow and father of Eanmund and Eadgils.

entities.name: Onela
entities.body: The Swedish king, brother of Ohthere and uncle of Eanmund and Eadgils.

entities.name: Eadgils
entities.body: The Swedish prince, son of Ohthere and brother of Eanmund.

entities.name: Eanmund
entities.body: The Swedish prince, son of Ohthere and brother of Eadgils.

entities.name: Herebald
entities.body: King Hrethel’s eldest son, brother of Hæthcyn and Hygelac.

entities.name: Hæthcyn
entities.body: Hrethel’s son and Hygelac’s brother, an earlier king of the Geats.

entities.name: Eofor
entities.body: The Geatish warrior in the war with Ongentheow, brother of Wulf.

entities.name: Dæghrefn
entities.body: The warrior of the Hugs in Beowulf’s account of his earlier battles.

entities.name: Weohstan
entities.body: Wiglaf’s father, also called Wihstan in this translation.

entities.name: Ælfhere
entities.body: The kinsman of Wiglaf named at his introduction.

entities.name: Wulf
entities.body: The Geatish warrior in the war with Ongentheow, brother of Eofor and son of Wonred.

entities.name: Wonred
entities.body: The father of Wulf and Eofor.

entities.name: The Merovingian ruler
entities.body: The Frankish ruler called Merewing in the account of Hygelac’s raid.

entities.name: The Danish coastguard
entities.body: Hrothgar’s coastal watchman, who questions Beowulf’s arriving party.

entities.name: The Geatish guide
entities.body: The seafaring man who shows Beowulf’s party the way before departure.

entities.name: The poet on the ride
entities.body: The Danish poet who praises Beowulf and recalls Sigmund during the ride from the mere.

entities.name: Hrothgar’s hall-singer
entities.body: The court performer who tells the Finn and Hildeburg story at the feast.

entities.name: The singer in Heorot
entities.body: The hall-singer whose song of creation is heard at the opening of the poem.

entities.name: Beowulf’s mother
entities.body: Hrethel’s daughter, wife of Ecgtheow and mother of Beowulf.

entities.name: Hildeburg’s son
entities.body: The son of Hildeburg and Finn in the hall-singer’s tale.

entities.name: Sigmund’s dragon
entities.body: The treasure-guarding dragon in the poet’s story of Sigmund.

entities.name: Unferth’s brothers
entities.body: The brothers whose deaths Beowulf raises in his argument with Unferth.

entities.name: The old Heathobard warrior
entities.body: The veteran whom Beowulf imagines stirring resentment at Ingeld’s wedding feast.

entities.name: The young Heathobard warrior
entities.body: The young man whom the imagined veteran urges to avenge his father.

entities.name: The young warrior’s father
entities.body: The fallen Heathobard whose sword appears in Beowulf’s imagined wedding dispute.

entities.name: Freaware’s Danish attendant
entities.body: The Danish warrior wearing inherited spoils in Beowulf’s imagined wedding dispute.

entities.name: The last survivor
entities.body: The unnamed man who deposits his vanished people’s treasures in the barrow.

entities.name: The fugitive servant
entities.body: The servant who takes a cup from the dragon’s hoard while seeking refuge.

entities.name: The servant’s master
entities.body: The lord from whom the fugitive servant seeks forgiveness with the stolen cup.

entities.name: The hanged son
entities.body: The young man on the gallows in the comparison used for Hrethel’s grief.

entities.name: The grieving father
entities.body: The old father in the gallows comparison, distinct from Hrethel himself.

entities.name: The Geatish messenger
entities.body: The warrior who reports news of the dragon fight to the waiting Geats.

entities.name: Ongentheow’s queen
entities.body: The Swedish king’s wife and mother of Onela and Ohthere in the war account.

entities.name: Hygelac’s daughter
entities.body: The king’s unnamed daughter, given in marriage to Eofor.

entities.name: The mourning woman
entities.body: The woman lamenting at Beowulf’s funeral, called a widow in this translation.

entities.name: Hrunting
entities.body: Unferth’s sword, lent to Beowulf for the journey into the mere.

entities.name: Nægling
entities.body: Beowulf’s sword in the fight with the dragon.

entities.name: Láfing
entities.body: The sword given to Hengest by Hun in this translation’s Finn episode.

entities.name: The Brosingmen’s necklace
entities.body: The legendary necklace carried off by Hama, used as a comparison for Beowulf’s gift.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The divine creator invoked by the poem’s narrator and speakers.

entities.name: Cain
entities.body: The biblical son of Adam and Eve, brother of Abel, whose line the poem associates with monsters.

entities.name: Abel
entities.body: Cain’s brother in the biblical story recalled by the narrator.

entities.name: Fate
entities.body: Destiny personified by the poet, called Weird or Wyrd as well as Fate.

entities.name: The Danes
entities.body: Hrothgar’s people, also called Scyldings and by several Danish epithets.

entities.name: The Geats
entities.body: Beowulf’s people, ruled by Hygelac when he sets out; also called Weders.

entities.name: The Scylfings
entities.body: The Swedish royal family and its people in the accounts of war with the Geats.

entities.name: The Wægmundings
entities.body: The family line shared by Beowulf and Wiglaf.

entities.name: The Wendels
entities.body: The people of whom Wulfgar is called a prince.

entities.name: The Wilfings
entities.body: Heatholaf’s people, involved in Ecgtheow’s feud.

entities.name: The Brondings
entities.body: Breca’s people.

entities.name: The Heathoremes
entities.body: The people whose coast Breca reaches in Unferth’s account of the swimming contest.

entities.name: The Finns
entities.body: The people whose land Beowulf says he reaches after the swimming ordeal.

entities.name: The Frisians
entities.body: The people of Finn in the lay and of the region raided by Hygelac.

entities.name: The Jutes
entities.body: The people called Jutemen in the Finn episode.

entities.name: The Franks
entities.body: The people encountered in the account of Hygelac’s fatal raid.

entities.name: The Hugs
entities.body: A name used here for the Franks, Dæghrefn’s people.

entities.name: The Hetwars
entities.body: The continental people fighting the Geats during Hygelac’s raid.

entities.name: The Heathobards
entities.body: Ingeld’s people, whose feud with the Danes is addressed through his betrothal.

entities.name: The Gepids
entities.body: A Germanic people named among possible sources of warriors.

entities.name: The giants
entities.body: The ancient beings whom the narrator places among the enemies of God.

entities.name: The elves
entities.body: The supernatural beings listed in the narrator’s account of Cain’s descendants.
